name: a table value goes back through String() (the original F3 defect)
why: The shipped bug, reverted exactly: dropping the `table` arm from _applyConfigSettings() lets a row array fall through to the String() arm, so [['series-releases','"Artist"']] becomes the string 'series-releases,"Artist"'. Lib.getTableRows() then rejects the non-array, the lazy seeders refill from the built-in defaults, and every hand-entered row is gone. The round-trip test must notice.
grep: every hand-entered table survives an export

name: the same defect, seen from the user's side
why: Identical edit to the entry above, scored against the user-visible test instead. Kept separate on purpose: the mechanism test reads GM storage, and a reader could reasonably ask whether `Array.isArray` is merely an internal detail. This shows the consequence — a column configured to start hidden comes back visible after an import, which is what a person would actually report.
grep: a column configured to start hidden still starts hidden

name: the Array.isArray guard is dropped, so a non-array is stored unmodified
why: The plausible over-simplification of the fix: 'tables are stored verbatim' taken to mean EVERY value offered for a table key. A corrupt or hand-edited file would then write a string into GM storage just as the original bug did, but via the new arm. The rejection test must notice — and must notice on the STORED VALUE, not just the invalid count, which is why that test asserts both.
grep: a non-array offered for a table key is rejected

name: the type:function skip is removed on import
why: Restores the pre-fix behaviour of writing sa_fn_edit_pinned_filter_list's internal method name into GM storage as if it were a user value. Only the import half of that test may notice — if the export assertion fails too, the two skips have been conflated.
grep: the export omits the type:function key

name: the type:function skip is removed on export
why: The export half of the same pair, mutated separately so each skip is its own guard. VZ_MBLibrary's own save/snapshot/reset loops skip ['divider','function','table']; this consumer's two loops skipped only 'divider', and both halves needed fixing.
grep: the export omits the type:function key

name: the unseeded-table drop is removed from _buildConfigJson()
why: EXPECTED TO PASS, recorded rather than left unmentioned. Without the explicit `continue`, an unseeded table key is assigned `undefined` — and JSON.stringify drops a property whose value is undefined, so the emitted file is byte-identical. The `continue` exists to make the behaviour deliberate and readable, not to change the output; no test can tell the two apart, and one that claimed to would be asserting something else.
grep: an unseeded table is dropped from the export

name: the table arm is placed AHEAD of the number arm
why: EXPECTED TO PASS. Arm order within the coercion chain is not load-bearing — the four type tests are mutually exclusive, so no value can reach two arms. Recorded so the next person to reorder them knows it was checked rather than discovering it by breaking something subtle later.
grep: every hand-entered table survives an export
